# T3.02-T3.05: P-frames

Done together in `src/enc.c`, after reading what the reference client sends for its P-frames (`docs/traces`,
frames 2 and 3 of `vttest-256x128-3f.log`):

- **T3.02 reference pictures.** The DPB is `num_refs + 1` recon slots (block-linear, 64 KB aligned). Each picture is
  reconstructed into a free slot (`SET_OUT_REF_PIC_LUMA/_CHROMA`), and its references are passed with
  `SET_IN_REF_PIC<slot>_LUMA/_CHROMA` (the method index is the slot, as the reference client does).
- **T3.03 numbering and lists.** `pic_type` 0, `frame_num` +1 (mod 256), `pic_order_cnt_lsb` = 2 x pictures since IDR
  (POC type 2). `l0[i]` = **2 x slot** (field-indexed: the reference client's frame 3 has `l0 = {2, 0}` for slots 1
  and 0), unused entries -2, `temp_dist_l0[i]` = i+1. **The slice's `num_ref_idx_active_override_flag` must be set on
  every P-frame**: with it clear on the first picture that has all `num_refs` references, the stream was undecodable
  from there on (2 or 3 refs; with 1 ref it never happens).
- **T3.04 per-frame state.** One colocated buffer (`SET_IN_COLOC_DATA` = `SET_OUT_COLOC_DATA`), two ME predictor
  buffers swapped every frame (`SET_IN_MEPRED_DATA` = last frame's output), the history buffer reused. The P-frame ME
  control turns on the temporal, spatial and constant hints with the reference client's stamps; `hint_type0..4` =
  0..4.
- **T3.05 `tools/encodeN`**: N frames of moving content (scrolling gradient and checkerboard, sweeping bar),
  `IDR_PERIOD=<n>` for periodic IDRs; `h264check` decodes the whole stream.

Results (Apple's software decoder, every picture compared with its source; QP I/P as given):

| stream | refs | avg luma / chroma | min luma | bitrate at 60 fps | encode avg |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 256x128, 60 frames, QP 26/26 | 1 | 47.97 / 46.87 dB | 46.99 | 0.28 Mbit/s | 0.05 ms |
| 256x128, 60 frames, QP 26/26 | 3 | 48.30 / 46.75 dB | 46.99 | 0.27 Mbit/s | 0.06 ms |
| 1920x1080, 60 frames, QP 26/28 | 1 | 46.55 / 45.38 dB | 46.09 | 11.9 Mbit/s | 1.46 ms |
| 1920x1080, 60 frames, QP 26/28 | 3 | 47.38 / 45.33 dB | 46.45 | 11.8 Mbit/s | 1.04 ms |
| 1920x1080, 60 frames, IDR every 20 | 2 | 46.94 / 45.58 dB | 46.43 | 12.5 Mbit/s | 1.07 ms |
| 3840x2160, 30 frames, QP 26/28 | 1 | 46.59 / 45.78 dB | 46.15 | 45.6 Mbit/s | 4.16 ms |

No decode errors, no drift (the last frames are as good as the first), 3 IDRs in the IDR-every-20 stream. P-frames
are mostly inter MBs (1080p: ~6550 of 8160). The per-frame maximum (3-5 ms at 1080p) is the first frame or two.
